title: Hosea Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hosea chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hosea Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hosea Chapter 14.

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:1 urge Israel to do?
options: Return unto the LORD thy God
questions.correctAnswer: Return unto the LORD thy God
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:1 clearly commands Israel to return unto the LORD their God because they have fallen by their iniquity.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:2, what should Israel take with them when they turn to the LORD?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:2 instructs Israel to take words with them and turn to the LORD, asking Him to take away all iniquity.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:3 states that Asshur will save Israel.
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:3 explicitly says that Asshur shall not save us, indicating that Israel should not rely on Asshur.

questions.question: In Hosea 14, what will Israel no longer say to the work of their hands?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:3 says Israel will no longer say to the work of their hands, 'Ye are our gods,' rejecting idolatry.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:2, what will Israel render to the LORD if He receives them graciously?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:2 states that if the LORD receives Israel graciously and takes away their iniquity, they will render the calves of their lips.

questions.question: Who does Hosea 14:3 say finds mercy in the LORD?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:3 says that in the LORD the fatherless findeth mercy.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:4 promises that the LORD will heal Israel's backsliding.
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:4 clearly states that the LORD will heal their backsliding and love them freely.

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:5 compare the LORD to in His care for Israel?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:5 says the LORD will be as the dew unto Israel, causing growth and strength.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:6, Israel's beauty shall be like what tree?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:6 compares Israel's beauty to the olive tree.

questions.question: In Hosea 14:7, those who dwell under Israel's shadow shall revive as what?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:7 states they shall revive as the corn and grow as the vine.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:8 says Ephraim will continue to worship idols.
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:8 says Ephraim will say, 'What have I to do any more with idols?' showing a rejection of idolatry.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:9, what will happen to transgressors?
options: They shall walk in the ways of the LORD
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:9 states that transgressors shall fall in the ways of the LORD.

questions.question: Which statement comes first in Hosea 14's instructions?
options: Return unto the LORD thy God
Say unto Him, Take away all iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: Return unto the LORD thy God
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:1 starts with the command to return unto the LORD thy God before the other instructions appear.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:4 declares that the LORD's anger is turned away from Israel.
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:4 states that the LORD will love Israel freely because His anger is turned away from them.

questions.question: What fragrance is Israel's smell compared to in Hosea 14:6?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:6 compares Israel’s smell to Lebanon.

medium.title: Hosea Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hosea Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:4, what will the LORD do to those who turn back to Him?
options: He will heal their backsliding and love them freely
He will punish them for their sins
He will give them riches and power
He will make them rulers over nations
questions.correctAnswer: He will heal their backsliding and love them freely
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:4 states that God promises to heal the backsliding of His people and love them freely, indicating restoration and forgiveness rather than punishment or material gain.

questions.question: How does Hosea 14:5 describe God's care for Israel after He heals them?
options: He will be as the dew unto Israel
He will give them a crown of gold
He will lead them into battle
questions.correctAnswer: He will be as the dew unto Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 5 uses the imagery of dew, showing gentle, life-giving care that causes Israel to grow and flourish, highlighting God’s nurturing nature after healing their backsliding (Hosea 14:4-5).

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Hosea 14:6 to describe the beauty and fragrance of Israel after God's blessing?
options: Olive tree and the smell as Lebanon
Rose bush and the scent of myrrh
Cedar tree and the fragrance of spices
Palm tree and the aroma of frankincense
questions.correctAnswer: Olive tree and the smell as Lebanon
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:6 compares Israel’s renewed beauty to the olive tree and its fragrance to the smell of Lebanon, emphasizing flourishing and pleasantness following God’s restoration (Hosea 14:5-6).

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:7 say will happen to those who live under Israel’s shadow?
options: They shall return and revive as the corn and grow as the vine
They shall be scattered and lost
They shall be conquered by their enemies
They shall wither like a dry leaf
questions.correctAnswer: They shall return and revive as the corn and grow as the vine
questions.explanation: Verse 7 promises revival and growth for those dwelling under Israel’s shadow, symbolizing the blessings and life found in God’s presence (Hosea 14:6-7).

questions.question: How does Hosea 14:4-5 teach us about God's forgiveness and provision in practical Christian living?
options: God freely loves and heals us, then nurtures our growth like dew on plants
God demands perfect obedience without mercy
God punishes us permanently for our failures
God only helps those who are wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: God freely loves and heals us, then nurtures our growth like dew on plants
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 reveal that God’s anger turns away when we repent, He heals us, and then provides nurturing care like dew, teaching us about forgiveness and ongoing spiritual growth.

questions.question: What lesson about humility and trust in God can be drawn from Hosea 14:3?
options: Do not rely on human power or idols, but find mercy in God
Trust in armies and horses for salvation
Worship the work of your own hands
Ignore God and trust only yourself
questions.correctAnswer: Do not rely on human power or idols, but find mercy in God
questions.explanation: Verse 3 warns against trusting Asshur, horses, or idols, emphasizing that only in God do the fatherless find mercy, teaching humility and reliance on God rather than human strength.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:8, what will Ephraim say after turning to the LORD?
options: "What have I to do any more with idols?"
"I will depend on the work of my hands"
questions.correctAnswer: "What have I to do any more with idols?"
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows Ephraim’s renunciation of idols after hearing and observing God’s ways, reflecting true repentance and trust in God alone.

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:9 say about the ways of the LORD and those who follow them?
options: The ways of the LORD are right, and the just shall walk in them
The ways of the LORD are hidden and mysterious
The LORD's ways lead to destruction
The just suffer when following the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The ways of the LORD are right, and the just shall walk in them
questions.explanation: Verse 9 emphasizes that God's ways are just and right, and those who are righteous will follow them successfully, while transgressors will fall.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:2 instructs believers to turn to the LORD with words asking for removal of iniquity and to receive them graciously.
questions.explanation: Verse 2 explicitly instructs to take words to the LORD, asking Him to take away all iniquity and receive them graciously, highlighting prayer and confession.

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:5 promise will happen if Israel returns and is healed as urged in verse 4?
options: Israel will grow as the lily and cast forth roots as Lebanon
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will grow as the lily and cast forth roots as Lebanon
questions.explanation: Verse 5 promises flourishing growth and deep rootedness for Israel as a result of God healing their backsliding as stated in verse 4, showing the blessing linked to repentance.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:1 calls Israel to return to the LORD because they have fallen by their iniquity.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 clearly calls Israel to return to God due to their fall caused by sin, emphasizing repentance as the first step toward restoration.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the connection between Hosea 14:6 and 14:7?
options: Verse 6 describes Israel’s beauty and scent, while verse 7 describes the revival and growth of those living under Israel’s influence
Verse 6 describes Israel’s destruction, verse 7 describes exile
Verse 6 warns of punishment, verse 7 encourages idolatry
Verse 6 and 7 both describe punishment for transgressors
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 6 describes Israel’s beauty and scent, while verse 7 describes the revival and growth of those living under Israel’s influence
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 together depict Israel’s flourishing beauty and the blessing on those dwelling under its shadow, showing a cause and effect relationship of God’s restoration.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue does Hosea 14:4 teach through God’s promise to heal and love freely?
questions.explanation: Verse 4’s promise to heal backsliding and love freely models God’s grace and forgiveness, encouraging believers to embrace these virtues in their lives.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:9 teaches that transgressors will succeed if they ignore the LORD's ways.
questions.explanation: Verse 9 clearly states that transgressors shall fall in the ways of the LORD, affirming that ignoring God's ways leads to failure, not success.

questions.question: A believer struggling with feelings of failure wants to know how Hosea 14 teaches about restoration. What biblical truth applies?
options: God promises to heal backsliding and love freely, turning away His anger
Failure is permanent and God will reject them
Only perfect people receive God's love
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to heal backsliding and love freely, turning away His anger
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:4 assures believers that God will heal their backsliding and love them freely, teaching that restoration is possible through repentance and God’s grace.

hard.title: Hosea Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hosea Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:7, what imagery is used to describe those who dwell under God's shadow?
options: They shall revive as the corn and grow as the vine
They shall be like the olive tree and smell as Lebanon
They shall be as the dew unto Israel
They shall be like horses and chariots
questions.correctAnswer: They shall revive as the corn and grow as the vine
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:7 specifically states that those who dwell under His shadow shall revive as the corn and grow as the vine, illustrating restoration and growth under God's protection.

questions.question: In Hosea 14:8, Ephraim compares himself to a green fir tree. What does this metaphor signify?
questions.explanation: The green fir tree symbolizes strength and ongoing fruitfulness, as Ephraim says, 'I am like a green fir tree. From me is thy fruit found,' indicating a renewed vitality (Hosea 14:8).

questions.question: Which phrase in Hosea 14:9 summarizes the moral direction for the just and the transgressors?
options: "For the ways of the LORD are right"
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:9 outlines that the ways of the LORD are right, the just will walk in them, but transgressors will fall, summarizing divine justice and moral consequence.

questions.question: Which nation or power is explicitly rejected as a savior in Hosea 14:3?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:3 clearly states, 'Asshur shall not save us,' rejecting reliance on Assyrian power for salvation.

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:4 promise God will do for Israel upon their return?
options: Heal their backsliding and love them freely
Make them rulers over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Heal their backsliding and love them freely
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:4 promises healing of Israel's backsliding and free love from God, emphasizing restoration and forgiveness.

questions.question: In Hosea 14:6, what are the two qualities attributed to Israel's branches?
options: Beauty like the olive tree and smell as Lebanon
Strong like cedar and bitter like wormwood
Green like the fir and sweet like honey
Dark as night and swift as the eagle
questions.correctAnswer: Beauty like the olive tree and smell as Lebanon
questions.explanation: Verse 14:6 describes Israel's branches as having beauty like the olive tree and a fragrant smell like Lebanon, symbolizing attractiveness and pleasantness.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:1, what is the reason Israel must return to the LORD?
options: Because they have fallen by their iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have fallen by their iniquity
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:1 states that Israel must return to God because they have fallen by their own iniquity, indicating sin as the cause of their downfall.

questions.question: Which of the following best represents the meaning of 'calves of our lips' in Hosea 14:2?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'calves of our lips' in Hosea 14:2 symbolizes spoken words of praise and confession offered to God instead of physical sacrifices.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:5 uses the metaphor of dew to describe God's blessing on Israel.
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:5 says, 'I will be as the dew unto Israel,' showing that God's blessing is gentle and life-giving like dew.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 14:3 encourages Israel to continue relying on the work of their own hands as gods.
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:3 explicitly states that Israel will no longer say to the work of their hands, 'Ye are our gods,' rejecting idolatry.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a similar theme of divine restoration and mercy as Hosea 14:4?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:3 speaks of God's everlasting love and mercy, paralleling Hosea 14:4's theme of healing and freely loving Israel.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Hosea 14:7 where growth and renewal imagery is repeated with parallel elements?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:7 uses parallelism by repeating similar ideas in balanced phrases about revival as corn and growth as the vine, enhancing poetic effect.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the righteous walking in God's ways as in Hosea 14:9?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:16 discusses walking in righteousness or sin, echoing Hosea 14:9's contrast between the just walking in God's ways and transgressors falling.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'backsliding' in Hosea 14:4 carries the meaning of:
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root for 'backsliding' (שׁוּב, shuv) implies turning away or rebellion against God, which Hosea 14:4 promises to heal.

questions.question: How does Hosea 14:8 signify a turning point in Israel's attitude toward idols?
options: Ephraim renounces idols and acknowledges fruitfulness from God
Ephraim blames idols for their misfortune
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim renounces idols and acknowledges fruitfulness from God
questions.explanation: In Hosea 14:8, Ephraim says, 'What have I to do any more with idols?' indicating a renouncement and a recognition that true fruitfulness comes from God.

theological.title: Hosea Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hosea Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is Israel commanded to do because of their sin according to Hosea 14:1?
options: Return unto the LORD thy God
questions.correctAnswer: Return unto the LORD thy God
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:1 commands Israel to return unto the LORD because they have fallen by their iniquity, emphasizing repentance as the first step to restoration.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:2, what should Israel take with them when turning to the LORD?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:2 instructs Israel to 'take with you words' when turning to God, highlighting the importance of confession and prayer in repentance.

questions.question: Which entity does Hosea 14:3 explicitly state will not save Israel?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:3 declares that Asshur shall not save Israel, rejecting reliance on foreign powers and idols for deliverance.

questions.question: What divine action does God promise to perform in Hosea 14:4?
questions.explanation: In Hosea 14:4, God promises to heal Israel’s backsliding and love them freely, showing His attribute of mercy and readiness to forgive.

questions.question: In Hosea 14:5, to what is God compared in relation to Israel?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:5 uses the metaphor of dew to describe God's refreshing and sustaining presence to Israel, emphasizing His nurturing care.

questions.question: What imagery in Hosea 14:6 represents Israel’s flourishing under God’s blessing?
options: Branches spreading and beauty like the olive tree
questions.correctAnswer: Branches spreading and beauty like the olive tree
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:6 describes Israel’s growth and beauty like the olive tree, symbolizing peace, prosperity, and divine blessing.

questions.question: According to Hosea 14:7, what will those dwelling under Israel's shadow experience?
options: Revival as the corn and growth as the vine
questions.correctAnswer: Revival as the corn and growth as the vine
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:7 promises that those under Israel’s shadow will revive and grow like crops and vines, symbolizing spiritual restoration and blessing.

questions.question: What does Ephraim declare about idols in Hosea 14:8?
options: What have I to do any more with idols?
Idols shall save us from enemies
Idols are more powerful than the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: What have I to do any more with idols?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:8 records Ephraim’s renunciation of idols, emphasizing repentance and recognition of the LORD's supremacy.

questions.question: What question does Hosea 14:9 pose regarding wisdom and understanding?
options: Who is wise, and he shall understand these things?
questions.correctAnswer: Who is wise, and he shall understand these things?
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:9 challenges the reader to gain wisdom and understanding of the ways of the LORD, highlighting the importance of discernment in walking righteously.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Hosea 14:4 and Hosea 14:9 regarding God's relationship with sinners and the righteous?
options: God heals backsliding and His ways are right, blessing the just and causing the fall of transgressors
God punishes all sinners equally and rewards none
God is indifferent to human actions
God favors the transgressors over the just
questions.correctAnswer: God heals backsliding and His ways are right, blessing the just and causing the fall of transgressors
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:4 shows God’s mercy in healing backsliding, while Hosea 14:9 affirms that the just walk in God’s right ways and transgressors fall, teaching divine justice and grace.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Hosea 14:5 and Hosea 14:6 about God's provision?
options: God provides growth, beauty, and sustenance to Israel like dew and fruitful trees
God leaves Israel barren and weak
God's blessings are conditional on human sacrifices
God's provision is limited to material wealth only
questions.correctAnswer: God provides growth, beauty, and sustenance to Israel like dew and fruitful trees
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:5-6 together depict God as a provider who nurtures Israel’s growth and beauty, symbolizing spiritual and physical flourishing under divine care.

questions.question: How does Hosea 14:3 reveal God's attribute of mercy?
options: In thee the fatherless findeth mercy
God is distant from human needs
God favors the strong over the weak
questions.correctAnswer: In thee the fatherless findeth mercy
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:3 states that in God the fatherless find mercy, demonstrating God's compassion and care for the vulnerable.

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:2 teach about the nature of true repentance?
options: It involves confessing sins and asking God to take away iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: It involves confessing sins and asking God to take away iniquity
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:2 emphasizes verbal confession and plea for forgiveness as essential aspects of repentance, not mere ritual or self-reliance.

questions.question: What narrative arc is reflected in Hosea 14:1-4 about Israel's restoration?
options: Repentance leads to divine healing and restoration
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance leads to divine healing and restoration
questions.explanation: The progression from call to repentance (14:1-2) to God’s promise to heal backsliding and love freely (14:4) fits the biblical theme of fall and redemption.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s ways are arbitrary and unjust. What does Hosea 14:9 teach about the nature of God's ways?
options: The ways of the LORD are right, just shall walk in them, transgressors shall fall
God’s ways are unpredictable and unfair
questions.correctAnswer: The ways of the LORD are right, just shall walk in them, transgressors shall fall
questions.explanation: Hosea 14:9 explicitly states that God's ways are right and just, affirming divine justice and moral order contrary to sceptical claims.
